subject: Post-call: Concurrency & rate limits — pilot / next steps
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Torres <eric.torres@finflux.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Concurrency & rate limits — pilot / next steps

Thanks for the call today — good alignment overall. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can scope a pilot: 

Summary (what we captured)
- Targets: 99th-percentile latency <= 120ms (sync text-gen), first-token streaming <= 400–500ms for live updates.
- Throughput: steady-state ~3k requests/minute during trading hours, burst to ~6k/min for 5–10m windows.
- Concurrency: expected 450–600 parallel streaming sessions during peak (user websockets), with an extra 20% headroom for short bursts.
- Connection behavior: apps will reuse long-lived WebSocket connections and multiplex requests per socket (we expect ~3 requests/conn on average).
- Data / compliance: standard SOC2 + data retention questions flagged (Marissa to follow up).

What Redwood can do (recommended approach)
- Pilot on Dedicated capacity with a reserved pool sized for 400 concurrent streaming sessions and configurable burst to 600 for 10m windows.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to cut per-token cost and improve tail latency.
- Use conservative multiplexing settings initially (2–4 parallel requests per socket) to reduce connection churn.
- Instrumenting: we'll expose per-route token/latency metrics and a webhook for SLO alerts.

Immediate asks for you
1) Fill the attached usage matrix (sheet: "Conn & Traffic Profile") with expected hourly distribution for a typical trading day.
2) Confirm whether burst windows can be tolerated as short as 5 minutes or need to be longer.
3) Share SOC2 point-of-contact so Marissa can deliver evidence and the security questionnaire.

Proposed Redwood offer for pilot (subject to your matrix):
- Reserved pool: 400 concurrent streaming sessions
- Baseline throughput allocation: 1,500 reqs/min (sustained)
- Burst allowance: +50% for up to 10 minutes (automatic fallback beyond)
- Pilot credits: 2 weeks on us to validate SLOs and tune multiplexing/caching

Next steps / timeline
- You return the usage matrix by EOD Thu (20 Aug).
- We size the Dedicated pool and send a short SOW and ratecard revision by Fri (21 Aug).
- Pilot starts as soon as contract signature & payment (target week of 31 Aug).

Attachments: usage matrix (xlsx), preliminary ratecard (pdf), call recording stub.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Marissa and Laura internally to get SOC2 artifacts ready.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0119
From: Eric Torres <eric.torres@finflux.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finflux.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & rate limits — pilot / next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciate the crisp summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Burst windows: typically we have micro-bursts of 2–3 minutes (spikes when market events hit) and sustained volatility windows of up to 15 minutes. Can Redwood handle both patterns without significant throttling?
2) Overages: if we hit burst beyond the allowance (e.g., a 20-minute spike), what is the behavior? Auto-throttle vs queue vs fail? Any temporary buffer/credit model?
3) Multiplexing: our frontend can multiplex requests but we need guidance on 'safe' parallelism per socket to avoid head-of-line blocking. Can you recommend concrete numbers based on the pilot offer?
4) We will fill the usage matrix — aiming to return it by Thu.

Also looping in Sarah (Eng Manager) for questions about streaming latency — Sarah, any specific p99 SLA you want to call out?

—Eric
Eric Torres | Head of Platform, FinFlux Corp
eric.torres@finflux.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 18:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Concurrency & rate limits — pilot / next steps (internal)

Internal notes + suggested commercial posture: 

- Concurrency offer (pilot): 400 reserved streaming sessions, burst to 600 for up to 10 minutes (aligns w/ Ben's note).
- Suggested safety caps: 4 parallel requests per socket default, with ability to increase to 6 after tuning. This avoids head-of-line blocking while preserving throughput.
- Overages: standard behavior = graceful throttling at the service-tier level (HTTP 429) with a token-bucket burst buffer. For enterprise pilots we can configure a short soft-queue (30s) for in-flight requests at additional cost.
- Credits: offer a 14-day pilot credit (we waive charges up to an agreed token cap). If FinFlux needs longer burst headroom during market stress, propose a one-time "burst credit" top-up.
- Ratecard: attach updated v2 with a line item for Dedicated reserved concurrency and a separate line for short soft-queue add-on.

Action items for Ben: include the above numbers in the reply to Eric, attach ratecard.

-Marissa
Director, Solutions & Security
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Torres <eric.torres@finflux.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & rate limits — pilot / next steps

Eric — thanks for the follow-up. Answers inline and a concrete pilot offer below.

On burst windows: Redwood's Dedicated pools support both short micro-bursts and longer volatility windows. Our standard policy is:
- Micro-bursts (<= 10m): allow burst to configured headroom (we recommended +50% above reserved).
- Extended spikes (> 10m): automatic graceful degradation to a lower-capacity tier or 429s; for pilots we can enable a soft-queue (30s buffer) for critical paths.

On overages: two options — auto-throttle (default) or soft-queue add-on. We offer a one-time burst credit to cover unexpected stress events during the pilot; after that, overages billed at post-paid overage rates on the attached ratecard.

On multiplexing: start with 3–4 logical requests per socket. From our experience with trading workloads, 3 parallel streams per socket balances latency and head-of-line risks. We can bump to 5–6 after observing p50/p95 tail characteristics in week 1 of pilot.

Concrete pilot offer (attached ratecard):
- Reserved: 400 concurrent streaming sessions (Dedicated)
- Baseline throughput: 1,500 reqs/min sustained
- Burst allowance: up to 600 concurrent for up to 10 minutes (auto-burst)
- Soft-queue add-on (opt-in): 30s in-flight buffer for critical routes (additional line item on ratecard)
- Pilot credits: 14 days waived up to 1.2M tokens

Next steps:
1) You return the filled usage matrix by Thu 20 Aug.
2) We send a short SOW + pilot MSA (standard enterprise terms) with the above numbers by Fri 21 Aug.
3) If SOC2 evidence looks good to you, legal can fast-track a short pilot amendment for signature.

Attaching: updated ratecard (redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf) and a blank usage matrix (as discussed).

Onwards — Ben
From: Eric Torres <eric.torres@finflux.com>

A couple quick asks before we sign:
- Can you send the SOC2 + recent penetration test summary to Sarah?
- Please add a one-time "burst credit" line (covering up to 25% above burst allowance for a single 24-hour event) to the SOW — we may need it for market-open anomalies.

If you can get those items in the SOW draft, we should be able to sign pilot MSA the week of Aug 31.

Thanks — Eric
